name: Bootsy Collins
hook: Left James Brown's band over a pay dispute at eighteen, then became the bassist whose sound defined George Clinton's mothership.
blurb: Bootsy Collins was eighteen when he and his brother Catfish joined James Brown's band in March 1970, right after most of Brown's musicians walked out in a pay dispute. Bootsy played bass on 'Sex Machine' and other hits before he and the rest of the new line-up, the J.B.'s, left over money problems of their own. George Clinton brought the Collins brothers into Funkadelic in 1972, and Bootsy rejoined Clinton's Parliament for 1974's 'Up for the Down Stroke'. Passing through the two biggest funk organisations on this map inside four years makes him a direct thread between them. His booming, playful bass, stretchy and syncopated and played as a lead voice rather than a background, became one of the most recognisable sounds in funk, and one of the most sampled and copied.
